name: Richat Structure (Eye of the Sahara)
description: A set of concentric rock rings about 40 km across, sitting in otherwise flat Saharan desert. From orbit it looks like a giant bullseye.
whyStrange: It looks like an impact crater but isn't one — it is an eroded dome of layered rock whose hard and soft bands weathered at different rates.

name: Lake Hillier
description: A small lake on Middle Island off Western Australia, separated from the deep-blue Southern Ocean by a thin strip of sand and eucalyptus forest.
whyStrange: Its water is often bubble-gum pink, coloured by salt-loving algae and bacteria; the shade changes with season and salinity, so imagery may show it pale.

name: Uffington White Horse
description: A highly stylised horse, 110 m long, cut into a chalk hillside in Oxfordshire and filled with crushed white chalk.
whyStrange: It is roughly 3,000 years old (Bronze Age) and only survives because locals have re-scoured the lines for centuries — and its abstract shape is best appreciated from the air.

name: Spiral Jetty
description: A 460 m coil of black basalt rock and mud winding into the Great Salt Lake, built by artist Robert Smithson in 1970.
whyStrange: Depending on lake levels it disappears underwater for years, then re-emerges encrusted with white salt crystals.

name: Mir Diamond Mine
description: An abandoned open-pit diamond mine in Siberia: a terraced hole about 525 m deep and 1.2 km wide, now partly flooded.
whyStrange: It is one of the largest excavated holes on Earth, and the vortex of air above it was long said to be a hazard for low-flying helicopters.

name: Darvaza Gas Crater (Door to Hell)
description: A collapsed crater in the Karakum Desert, about 70 m wide, where natural gas has been burning continuously for decades.
whyStrange: It is believed to have been set alight deliberately during Soviet-era drilling to burn off the gas — and it simply never went out.

name: The Boneyard at Davis–Monthan
description: Thousands of retired military aircraft parked in tidy rows on the Arizona desert, stored by the 309th Aerospace Maintenance and Regeneration Group.
whyStrange: The dry air and alkaline soil slow corrosion, so it doubles as an enormous outdoor parts warehouse — the planes look like a toy collection from above.

name: Gobi Desert Grids
description: Huge patterns of pale lines — zigzags, grids and radiating spokes — scraped across the desert of Gansu province.
whyStrange: They are widely believed to be calibration targets for spy-satellite cameras, but no official explanation has ever been given.

name: Great Blue Hole
description: A near-perfect circle of deep indigo water about 300 m across, ringed by the pale coral of Lighthouse Reef.
whyStrange: It is a sinkhole that formed on dry land during the last ice age and was drowned when sea levels rose; stalactites still hang inside it.

name: Fly Geyser
description: A small, multicoloured mound in the Nevada desert that sprays hot water from several vents, surrounded by terraced pools.
whyStrange: It is accidental: a 1960s well drilling punctured a geothermal pocket, and dissolved minerals have been building the brightly coloured cone ever since.

name: Sedan Crater
description: A 390 m wide, 100 m deep crater on the Nevada National Security Site.
whyStrange: It was blasted in 1962 by a 104-kiloton nuclear test exploring whether bombs could be used for excavation — it is the largest man-made crater in the US.

name: Huangyangtan Terrain Model
description: A walled compound near Yinchuan holding a roughly 900 × 700 m scale model of mountainous terrain.
whyStrange: Satellite watchers matched it to the disputed Aksai Chin region on the China–India border; its purpose is presumed to be military training.

name: Groom Lake (Area 51)
description: A dry lakebed in the Nevada desert flanked by long runways, hangars and support buildings.
whyStrange: It is the famously secretive Area 51 test site — long denied officially and the subject of endless UFO lore.

name: Cretto di Burri
description: A field of white concrete blocks covering the ruins of old Gibellina in Sicily, cut through by narrow walkable lanes.
whyStrange: Artist Alberto Burri entombed the earthquake-destroyed town under concrete; the lanes follow the old streets, making it a town-sized memorial.

name: Galešnjak (Island of Love)
description: A tiny uninhabited island in the Pašman Channel off the Dalmatian coast.
whyStrange: It is naturally shaped like an almost perfect heart — first noticed when the island appeared in aerial imagery.

name: The World Islands
description: Around 300 artificial islands off Dubai, arranged to form a map of the world's continents.
whyStrange: Built from dredged sand in the 2000s, most of the islands remain undeveloped years later, slowly reshaped by the sea.

name: Duga Radar
description: A rusting wall of antennas, roughly 150 m tall and 500 m long, hidden in the forest of the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone.
whyStrange: This Soviet over-the-horizon radar broadcast a repetitive tapping signal worldwide, nicknamed the 'Russian Woodpecker' by radio listeners.

name: Bourtange Star Fort
description: A five-pointed star fortress surrounded by double moats in the north-east of the Netherlands.
whyStrange: Restored to its 18th-century layout, the whole village sits inside a geometric star that only really makes sense from above.

name: Grand Prismatic Spring
description: The largest hot spring in the United States, in Yellowstone National Park, about 110 m across.
whyStrange: Bands of heat-loving microbes paint it in rings from deep blue through green and yellow to orange — like a giant eye.

name: Kolmanskop Ghost Town
description: A former diamond-mining town in the Namib Desert, abandoned in the 1950s.
whyStrange: Sand dunes have marched into the houses: rooms are filled to the windowsills with sand while the buildings still stand.

name: Dallol Hydrothermal Field
description: A hydrothermal field in the Danakil Depression, more than 100 m below sea level.
whyStrange: Acidic hot springs and salt deposits create neon yellow, green and orange pools — one of the most alien-looking places on the planet.

name: Palmanova
description: A Renaissance town in Friuli built inside a nine-pointed star of fortifications, with streets radiating from a hexagonal central square.
whyStrange: It was planned from scratch in 1593 as an 'ideal city' — its perfect radial symmetry is unmistakable from above.

name: Lake Retba (Lac Rose)
description: A shallow, very salty lake just behind the dunes of Senegal's Atlantic coast, near Dakar.
whyStrange: Its water can turn strawberry pink thanks to salt-loving algae, especially in the dry season; workers harvest salt from its bed by hand.

name: Hashima (Battleship Island)
description: A small island off Nagasaki entirely covered in concrete apartment blocks and a sea wall.
whyStrange: It once housed a coal-mining community among the densest populations ever recorded, then was abandoned overnight in 1974; its silhouette resembles a warship.

name: Bingham Canyon Mine
description: A vast open-pit copper mine near Salt Lake City, over 4 km wide and around 1.2 km deep.
whyStrange: Its stepped terraces form a giant spiral amphitheatre — it is one of the largest human-made excavations in the world.

name: Nazca Lines — Hummingbird
description: One of the Nazca geoglyphs: a hummingbird roughly 90 m long, drawn by removing dark surface stones to reveal lighter ground.
whyStrange: Made around 2,000 years ago, the figures are hard to recognise from the ground; the surrounding plain is criss-crossed by long straight lines and trapezoids visible in imagery.
